text: Borealis (2022) encodes its 216 modes as a train of squeezed-light pulses and entangles them using three fiber delay loops. What are the three loop delays, and what do they provide?
choices: Delays of tau, 2tau, and 4tau, giving binary-tree connectivity
Delays of tau, 6tau, and 36tau, giving programmable couplings at three ranges
Delays of 36tau, 216tau, and 1296tau, one loop per mode
A single loop of tau reused 216 times, giving nearest-neighbor coupling only
explanation: Borealis uses loops of delay tau, 6tau, and 36tau with programmable beam splitters, coupling each pulse to neighbors 1, 6, and 36 time-bins away — a 3D topology unrolled in time. Choice 0 uses the wrong (binary) delays; choice 2 invents per-mode loops (the whole economy is that one source plus three loops replaces thousands of elements); choice 3 keeps only the shortest loop and loses the multi-range programmability.
